answer.summary: Converts a 6-character date string (JJMMTT) into an 8-character format (JJJJMMTT) by prepending a century prefix. It prepends '19' if the year part is 94 or higher, otherwise it prepends '20'. The routine is marked as unused since the year 2000.

rules.text: If the first two characters of the input date (SUBSTR(P#D6,1,2)) are greater than or equal to the constant D#ALT_JJ ('94'), the function returns the concatenation of D#ALT_JH ('19') and the input P#D6.
If the first two characters of the input date are less than D#ALT_JJ ('94'), the function returns the concatenation of the literal string '20' and the input P#D6.
